title: Saka faces crossroads between expectations and reality
seoTitle: Saka faces crossroads of expectations and reality
subtitle: What is driving the discussion about the forward's future at Arsenal
excerpt: Bukayo Saka is at the center of a discussion blending performance expectations and criticism over Arsenal's lack of an elite striker.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Arsenal have entered the peak of the season with expectations of maintaining their supremacy in the Premier League, but the lack of a standout striker has been a topic of debate. Bukayo Saka, who turns 25 this weekend, is at the center of the discussion, with analysts questioning whether he can elevate the team to the level of an elite forward.

Criticism over the lack of a super-striker

Pundits point out that, despite winning the Premier League last year, Arsenal lack a forward who stands out in major competitions. The pursuit of players like Vinícius Júnior, Julián Álvarez, and Morgan Rogers during the transfer window did not result in signings, leaving the team with an attacking line considered insufficient by some.

Saka's performance in recent years

In 2022 and 2024, Saka recorded 26 and 28 combined goals and assists in the Premier League, respectively. However, last season, his output dropped to 14 goals and 9 assists, reflecting a stagnation in his performance. This is partly due to injuries the player has suffered in recent years.

Ambitious target expectations

Thierry Henry, former Arsenal player, has set a challenge for Saka: to reach 15 goals and 15 assists in the current season. Only three players – Henry, Eden Hazard, and Mohamed Salah – have ever achieved this feat in a single 38-game Premier League campaign.

Impact on national teams

Saka participated in England's World Cup, where he scored five goals, including a hat-trick in the third-place playoff against France. His international performance has been seen as a motivator to prevent similar situations from occurring in future tournaments.

Future prospects

With six years of his career still ahead of him, Saka has the opportunity to become one of the most feared forwards in the world. If he achieves his targets, he could change the perception of Arsenal as a team without an elite striker, transforming the club into an even stronger competitor up front.

With information from The Telegraph, Football London.
